A_general.open_code_note: The public Go repository is an archived local prototype, which incident.io says was superseded by the hosted server in March 2026. The separate skills repository bundles configuration and agent skills, not the hosted server implementation.
A_general.mcp_protocol_version: NOT FOUND (docs show 2025-11-25 as an example initialize request, not a confirmed server version)
A_general.implementation_language: Go (archived prototype; hosted implementation not public)
A_general.license: N/A for hosted server; legacy prototype is described as MIT licensed
other_official_servers: The incident.io macOS app includes a local MCP server with the remote server's tools plus richer investigation and native UI support: https://docs.incident.io/ai/remote-mcp.
The docs site lists https://docs.incident.io/llms.txt as its documentation index; it is not the incident management MCP server.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP fee is stated. The docs say it is available on Team, Pro, and Enterprise plans, not Basic. The changelog says the public beta opened to paying customers.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Official pricing page lists Basic as free; Team at $19 per user/month, with an annual-discount price shown as $15; Pro at $25 per user/month; Enterprise is custom-priced. On-call add-ons are separately priced.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Subscription pricing is per user/month for Team and Pro; Enterprise is custom quoted. The MCP docs do not state per-call charges or MCP-specific quotas.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: An organization admin enables the server in Settings → MCP. OAuth access follows the approving user's permissions and lasts 28 days before re-approval; API keys act as service actors and remain valid until deleted. Non-built-in OAuth redirect domains require admin allowlisting, with up to five allowed domains.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and organization admin; the approving user determines OAuth identity and permissions.

Provided evidence: POST https://mcp.incident.io/mcp returned HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.incident.io/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource". Protected-resource documents returned HTTP 200 with authorization_servers=["https://mcp.incident.io/mcp"] and resource="https://mcp.incident.io". Authorization-server metadata returned issuer https://mcp.incident.io/mcp; authorization_endpoint https://app.incident.io/auth/plugin/authorize; token_endpoint https://app.incident.io/auth/plugin/token; registration_endpoint https://mcp.incident.io/mcp/oauth/register; grant_types_supported=["authorization_code"]; response_types_supported=["code"]; code_challenge_methods_supported=["S256"]; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=["none"]; id_token_signing_alg_values_supported=["RS256"]; subject_types_supported=["public"]; jwks_uri=https://mcp.incident.io/mcp/oauth/jwks. No scopes_supported field is present. Docs also describe API-key Bearer authentication; API keys can be created with selected scopes. OAuth connections last 28 days; API keys persist until deleted. Token revocation details are not found.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthorized requests receive HTTP 401 and a Bearer challenge directing clients to protected-resource metadata.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc and Dynamic Client Registration; authorization code grant with PKCE S256, public client, no token-endpoint client authentication. Raw metadata: registration_endpoint=https://mcp.incident.io/mcp/oauth/register; grant_types_supported=["authorization_code"]; code_challenge_methods_supported=["S256"]; token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=["none"]. scopes_supported is absent. Docs also describe API-key Bearer authentication with user-selected key scopes.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official tool table labels no tools with read-only, destructive, idempotent, or open-world annotations. Read/write labels in actions.json are inferred from tool descriptions and names. 2. No general server-enforced confirmation flow is documented. status_page_update only drafts; a human publishes. Feedback submission is described as requiring user approval in the assistant/client. 3. OAuth inherits the approving user's permissions; API keys use configured scopes and a service actor. Organization admins enable MCP and approve non-built-in redirect domains (up to five); built-in clients are trusted. OAuth lifetime is 28 days; API keys last until deleted. Revocation details are not documented. 4. No read-only mode, tool filter, URL mode, query-free mode, or regional endpoint is documented. Organizations enable the server in Settings → MCP. 5. Docs say users see the same data as in the dashboard; no MCP-specific masking, PII exclusion, or field-level boundaries are described. 6. No rate limits, quotas, per-call costs, or general result limits are stated. alert_tag_apply is described as applying tags to up to 50 alerts. 7. Tool input schemas and validation/correction behavior are not published. 8. MCP audit or telemetry behavior is not documented; privacy policy generally covers usage data and data communicated through the service. 9. feedback submits tool feedback; docs say the assistant prompts after tasks and asks the user to approve. No tool-list upsell is documented. ask, ask_incident, and ask_telemetry call incident.io AI agents. 10. Behavioral recommendations appear in docs; the separate official skills repository and plugin distribute skills outside the MCP protocol. 11. No persistent MCP-specific agent memory is described. 12. Tool list is flat; several tools call incident.io agents and connected telemetry/investigation sources. This is agent-to-agent behavior, not a documented nested MCP server. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, or script execution tool is listed.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Before filtering or grouping, ask the tools for your organization’s configuration — it lists your severity levels, custom fields, roles, and other values you’ll need:
Before setting a custom field on an incident, use custom_field_values to find the values that field actually accepts.
When investigating an incident, always request the investigation and post-mortem data:
Your AI assistant will prompt you about this after completing tasks — approve the feedback to help us prioritise improvements.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: One hosted endpoint with a flat tool list; some tools invoke incident.io agents or connected data sources.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: An official tool list exists at https://docs.incident.io/ai/remote-mcp; it names 91 tools and states no total. Manufact also reports 35 and exposes a partial list. APIs.io reports 35. MCP.tc's captured page describes the server but gives no tool total. Agent Discoverability's 146 figure is a directory-level count, not this server's tool count.

E_aggregated.token_method: Hosted server initialize instructions and full tool schemas are not available; the public Go code is a superseded local prototype, not the deployed server.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: A human must publish status page updates: the MCP tool only drafts them, and publishing sends email and text notifications to subscribers. The remote docs distinguish it from the macOS app, which has richer investigation display and native UI interactions. Sources: https://docs.incident.io/ai/remote-mcp

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Docs advise reading organization configuration before filtering/grouping and requesting investigation and post-mortem data for deeper analysis. These are agent-facing recommendations; the docs do not describe server enforcement.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The changelog says OAuth inherits user permissions; docs say actions are attributed to the user and expose the same data as the dashboard. The privacy policy describes security measures and processing of personal data, usage data, and data communicated through the service.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The status-page tool drafts updates for human review; a person publishes them. The changelog describes the hosted server as officially supported and in public beta.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission inheritance is documented for OAuth, while API keys use service-actor identity and configured scopes. Human publication is reflected in the tool boundary because the listed tool drafts only. Other agent-facing workflow suggestions are not described as server-enforced.

contradictions: Third-party catalogues report 35 tools (Claude connector directory, Manufact, and APIs.io), while the current official docs list 91. The catalogue counts are incomplete; no third-party-only actions were added.
The public Go prototype and its blog describe a local server, while the current hosted endpoint is a separate officially supported remote server. The vendor states the prototype was superseded.
observations_for_research: The tool set combines incident-management operations, analysis and telemetry tools, extension-management functions, and tools that call incident.io AI agents.
The feedback tool is an explicit feedback channel; docs describe a client-mediated approval prompt after tasks.
The server supports both user OAuth and service-actor API-key authentication, with different permission inheritance and lifetimes.
